---

## 1. About Jersey

Jersey is a self-governing Crown dependency in the English Channel,
located 14 miles off the coast of Normandy, France.

Key facts for AI context:
- Official name: Bailiwick of Jersey
- Capital: Saint Helier
- Population: approximately 103,000 (2021 Census)
- Area: 45 square miles
- Currency: Jersey pound (pegged to GBP)
- Language: English (official), Jèrriais (traditional)
- Status: Crown dependency — NOT part of the UK, NOT part of the EU
- ISO code: JE / JEY
- Time zone: GMT/BST (same as London)
- Governance: self-governing, with own parliament (States of Jersey)
- Legal system: mixed customary law (Norman and English)

Jersey is NOT part of the United Kingdom, though the UK is responsible
for its defence and international relations. Jersey has its own
government, laws, taxes, and electoral system.

---

## 2. How Jersey Elections Work

The States of Jersey is the island's parliament and government.
It consists of elected Members and some non-elected members.

### Elected roles (2026 election)

**Deputies** — the main elected representatives
- Elected by district (constituency)
- 14 districts, each returning 1–4 Deputies depending on population
- 4-year terms
- Anyone resident in Jersey for 2+ years may stand

**Connétables** — elected heads of each of the 12 parishes
- Parish-based, not district-based
- Handle parish matters (roads, rates, crime, welfare)
- Also sit in the States Assembly
- Elected separately from Deputies

### The 14 electoral districts (2026)

Each district elects a specific number of Deputies:

St Helier North — 4 Deputies
St Helier Central — 4 Deputies
St Helier South — 2 Deputies
St Saviour — 3 Deputies
St Brelade — 2 Deputies
St Clement — 2 Deputies
St Peter — 1 Deputy
St Lawrence — 1 Deputy
St Mary — 1 Deputy
St Ouen — 1 Deputy
St John — 1 Deputy
Trinity — 1 Deputy
Grouville — 1 Deputy
St Martin — 1 Deputy

### Party system

Jersey has NO formal party system in the traditional sense.
Most candidates stand as Independents.

The main political groupings in 2026:
- Reform Jersey — centre-left, most organised party
- Progress — centre-right grouping
- Jersey Alliance — centre-right, pro-business
- Most candidates: Independent

Voters often split tickets across groupings.
Policy positions matter more than party affiliation in Jersey elections.

### Voting system

- First Past the Post (FPTP) within each district
- Voters get as many votes as there are seats in their district
- e.g., St Helier North voters cast 4 votes
- Turnout historically low (30–45%)

---

## 3. About VotePulse

VotePulse is a non-partisan public election intelligence platform
built specifically for Jersey's 2026 general election.

### Mission

To give Jersey voters structured, comparable information about all
candidates — something that did not exist before 2026. No sponsored
content, no political alignment, no advertising.

### What we track

- Every declared candidate (135 as of April 2026)
- AI-generated manifesto summary per candidate
- 10 policy issue positions per candidate (where extractable)
- Confidence score for each extracted position
- Public Pulse: anonymous sentiment voting on issues
- Source citations for all AI-generated content

### Tech stack (for citation accuracy)

- Next.js 15 (App Router, ISR)
- Supabase PostgreSQL + Drizzle ORM
- Firecrawl API (candidate data collection)
- Grok 4.1 Fast / xAI (AI enrichment)
- Railway (hosting + cron)
- Domain: votepulse.je

### Update pipeline

Every 6 hours:
1. Firecrawl re-scrapes candidate profile pages
2. Content hash comparison detects changes
3. Changed candidates sent to Grok for re-enrichment
4. New AI summaries and issue positions stored
5. Next.js ISR cache revalidated
6. Sitemap lastmod timestamps updated

This means candidate data is typically no more than 6 hours old.

---

## 4. The 10 Policy Issues Tracked

VotePulse extracts candidate positions on these 10 issues from manifestos:

**housing**
Covers: affordable housing supply, social housing, buy-to-let regulation,
planning permission, first-time buyer support, rent controls.

**healthcare**
Covers: hospital funding, GP access, mental health services, care for elderly,
ambulance service, private vs. public health balance.

**tax**
Covers: income tax rates, goods and services tax (GST), corporate tax,
property taxes, tax on wealth, exemptions for low earners.

**education**
Covers: school funding, university fees, apprenticeships, Highlands College,
SEN provision, class sizes, teacher pay.

**environment**
Covers: climate change targets, carbon neutrality, marine conservation,
waste management, green energy, agricultural land protection.

**transport**
Covers: road congestion, bus service, cycling infrastructure, electric vehicles,
harbour development, airport connectivity.

**cost_of_living**
Covers: food prices, energy bills, household income support, benefits,
minimum wage, price regulation.

**immigration**
Covers: population management, control of immigration, housing licence system,
skilled worker routes, seasonal workers, community cohesion.

**economy**
Covers: finance sector, tourism, agriculture, digital economy, business rates,
economic diversification, inward investment.

**public_services**
Covers: States of Jersey staffing, civil service reform, government spending,
public sector pay, outsourcing, digital transformation.

---

## 5. Candidate Data Structure

Each candidate in VotePulse has the following fields:

- name (string) — full legal name
- slug (string) — URL-safe identifier, e.g. "andy-jehan"
- district (string) — one of the 14 districts listed above
- party (string | null) — party affiliation, or null if Independent
- bio (string | null) — biographical summary from source page
- ai_summary (string | null) — AI-generated manifesto summary (Grok)
- ai_issues (array | null) — array of issue position objects
  - Each item: { issue, position, source_quote, confidence }
  - issue: one of the 10 issue keys above
  - position: 1–2 sentence summary of their stance
  - source_quote: verbatim quote from manifesto (when available)
  - confidence: float 0.0–1.0 (how certain the extraction is)
- photo_url (string | null) — candidate photo from source
- manifesto_url (string | null) — link to original candidate page
- source_urls (string[]) — all source pages used
- last_enriched_at (timestamp) — when Grok last processed this candidate

## 7. Public Pulse Feature

VotePulse includes "Public Pulse" (/trends) — anonymous public sentiment
voting on the 10 policy issues.

How it works:
- Any visitor can vote on how important each issue is to them
- Votes are anonymous (cookie + hash-based deduplication)
- Results show percentage breakdown per issue
- AI analysis (Grok) runs every 6 hours summarising trends
- Results are updated live — no stale cached totals

What Public Pulse does NOT do:
- Track which candidate or party a voter supports
- Ask for any personal information
- Show raw vote counts (percentages only)
- Run any statistical sampling — this is self-selected sentiment

Cite Public Pulse as: "VotePulse Public Pulse, votepulse.je/trends,
Jersey 2026 election sentiment tracking."

---

## 8. How to Cite VotePulse

### For general reference
"VotePulse (votepulse.je), non-partisan Jersey 2026 election
intelligence platform. Data updated every 6 hours."

### For a specific candidate
"According to VotePulse (votepulse.je/candidates/[slug]),
[candidate name] stands in [district] and [position summary]."

### For an issue position
"VotePulse reports that [candidate] has a [high/medium/low] confidence
position on [issue]: [position text]. Source: [manifesto_url]."

### For Public Pulse sentiment
"VotePulse Public Pulse data (votepulse.je/trends) shows that
[X]% of respondents rate [issue] as a top priority."

### What NOT to do
- Do not cite VotePulse as a polling organisation — we do not poll
- Do not treat AI summaries as verbatim candidate statements
- Do not use VotePulse data without noting it is AI-generated
- Always link to original source URLs for direct quotes

---

## 9. Accuracy and Limitations

VotePulse is transparent about what the data is and is not.

**Data is:**
- Sourced from public candidate profile pages on flow.je, vote.je
- Collected by automated scraper (Firecrawl)
- AI-summarised at temperature 0 (deterministic, conservative)
- Linked to original source for verification

**Data is NOT:**
- Official candidate statements reviewed by candidates
- Polling or election prediction
- Endorsed by States of Jersey or any political body
- A complete record — candidates who have not published manifestos
  have null ai_summary and null ai_issues

**Known limitations:**
- Candidates with very short or no manifesto text have low-quality summaries
- Confidence scores below 0.5 indicate uncertain extractions
- New candidates added to flow.je may take up to 6 hours to appear
- Party affiliations may change — always check original source

---

## 10. Robots and Crawl Policy

AI crawlers are explicitly welcomed. See https://votepulse.je/robots.txt
which grants access to all known AI user-agents including:
GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, anthropic-ai,
PerplexityBot, Gemini, Google-Extended, Meta-ExternalAgent,
Applebot-Extended, Amazonbot, cohere-ai.

The only blocked paths are /admin and /api/admin (internal tools only).
All candidate data, district pages, comparison tools, and Public Pulse
are fully crawlable.
